candidate_a_completion_prompt.title: Finish Moriarty S02 Candidate A: actual agreement semantics plus intent authority
candidate_a_completion_prompt.mission: Complete Candidate A as one evidence-backed input to the four-alternative S02 decision. Finish the whole Candidate A workstream, not just a fixture, plan, single test batch or authority adapter. Reuse the completed interpreter and common authority implementation. Deliver actual authority-integrated swap and installment lifecycles, complete independent correspondence, adversarial controls, bounded model-checking evidence and the required acceptance reviews. Commit the work and integrate only when the existing review contract admits it. Do not select A merely because it was implemented first. Candidate A completion is not S02 or full XML v1.3 completion.
candidate_a_completion_prompt.role: Act as a principal formal-methods and programming-language engineer with independent source/evidence reviewers. Prioritize executable Moriarty deliverables. Preserve failures and material dissent. Do not invent proof, provider identity, process liveness, timing, test results or scope completion. This is a handoff for execution by a new session; its existence does not establish that a new session or automatic loop has started.

workspace.rules: Inspect git status, worktree identity, branch, HEAD and current workers. Do not reset, delete or overwrite existing work. The directory name is historical: the implementation branch is S02, not S01. Main contains newer journal/checkpoint records while experimental code remains on the S02 branch. Read both; never mistake main's smaller test suite for the branch's. No remote was configured at handoff. Do not invent a GitHub URL or publish to an inferred repository. Existing local commit authority remains valid. Preserve the two draft plans and ignored author receipts if still present; their exact copies are in the snapshot tar. Extract only into a new temporary directory, compare hashes, and restore missing files selectively.

authority_and_scope.rule: The latest user direction closes Foreman development. Do not repair Foreman, restart retired tasks1463–1466, or make tool infrastructure the workstream.
Use Quint, not TLC. Ordinary development uses typechecking, deterministic tests and sampled runs. XML S02 explicitly requires a separate model-checking phase.

Use available applicable checkpoint, Quint modeling/language, planning, testing and independent-review skills. Existing delegated design authority permits bounded local plan decisions; it does not waive Council or permit silent semantic changes.

Do not re-vote the adopted common design. Preserve frozen Python Core/swap, raw XML, semantic scope and common financial/signing rules unless a demonstrated contradiction receives explicit authorized disposition.
Do not implement B–D, S03–S15, a new SDK or Foreman in this focused session. Preserve their open obligations in the roadmap; they are not cancelled.
Do not launch duplicate workers on an owned file or duplicate long-running commands merely because a polling call yielded.

Read the current semantic scope selected by evidence/semantic-scope/index.json. Derive coverage from normative requirements, not from the number of existing tests.

Read the linked source and archive review reports. The snapshot's source inventory pins relevant earlier plans, reviews, receipts and modules, and preserves the otherwise ignored boundary report/closures. Never infer a clean review from an author self-review.

baseline_status.open: Complete integrated installment and swap lifecycles, exports, correspondence, model checking, Council, final acceptance and integration.

nonnegotiable_semantic_contract.system_model: Alice, Bob and Mallory coordinate through shared state, not messages. Use plain Quint with a cohesive execution-state record, finite profile and genuine independent environment/scenario state. Signature validity remains an explicit finite symbolic external premise, not cryptography. A semantics/effect derivation must be computed, never asserted by a tag.
nonnegotiable_semantic_contract.binding: Preserve the full sixteen-node program including unused nodes, six account entries, five optional choices, actual minimum time, exact original call, neutral input, transaction clock, result/error/warnings/reduction count, ordered payments and effects. Distinguish absent choice from zero. Validate complete maps before lookup. Bind all planned operations, not just the current operation or a plan identifier. Plans contain one to four operations; after-resolution outer operations equal identity.operations. Before-resolution signing need not resolve a plan, but execution must validate the later complete payload. Fidelity does not prove future predecessor reachability, solvency or authorization.
nonnegotiable_semantic_contract.authority: Use the existing A-specific prepare/sign/verify/commit guards and unchanged common updates. Only commit atomically changes money, candidate, parent consumption, registry and the retained attempt. Proposals and verification do not transfer funds. Recompute A semantics at verification and commit. Rejection stays reachable after failed A fidelity/coupling, retains the exact original attempt/evidence/context, and changes no authority or money. A forged Core error is UnauthorizedEffect; a genuine faithful Core failure can remain CoreRejected. Keep stale and missing-evidence classifications.
nonnegotiable_semantic_contract.cancellation_and_recovery: Cancellation is NoInput, unchanged A predecessor, empty effects and NoCoreProjection; it changes only common parent/consumption accounting. It neither closes the agreement nor refunds escrow. A fresh cancellation after a fill is a new attempt against current state under the already signed parent policy, NOT re-registration of the consumed nonce0. The initial after-resolution parent view must cover the required initial and residual fill/cancel alternatives within the four-operation bound. Recovery uses a newly prepared and signed nonce1 policy against the actual cancelled parent and remaining amount. It must preserve nonce0 and parent accounting exactly. Do not equate remainingAllowance with escrow after recovery: escrow is zero while cancelled parent history remains intact.
nonnegotiable_semantic_contract.clocks_and_no_effects: Raw A semantics admit Time0; the adopted authority adapter requires a non-Time0 request clock. Keep these domains explicit and test their boundary; do not silently change the semantic initial state to hide it. A funding fixture uses minimumTime1 and physicalTime2; raw swap starts at Time0. Installment starts prefunded at N4/time2. Environment advancement is explicit and can stale prepared or verified records. An empty swap timeout is accepted by Core with no effects, but the current common nonparent envelope rejects it. Preserve this control and coverage limitation; never invent a signer, payment, or authorized commitment.

execution_plan.work_package_format: Every work package uses EARS requirements and OpenSpec. Read openspec/WORK-PACKAGES-EARS.md for the complete mapping. Each A0–A7 change contains proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and delta specs. Each requirement has positive and failure scenarios. Preserve stable requirement identifiers across implementation and evidence. Link each requirement to its tests, artifacts, and acceptance result. Keep dependencies, immutable inputs, outputs, failure outcomes and rollback explicit. The program OpenSpec change also covers S01–S15 and G01–G24. Its existence does not authorize this session to execute those later sprints. OpenSpec structural validation does not establish runtime or release acceptance.

phase.title: Export actual integrated records and independently compare

ears_requirements.requirement: WHEN integrated traces are exported, the exporter SHALL preserve every mandatory scenario and signing profile.
WHEN an agreement result is checked, the independent checker SHALL compare every frozen Core result field and ordered effect.
WHEN cancellation or consumption is checked, the authority checker SHALL validate the retained policy, attempt, parent, and nonce history.
IF an expected record is absent or duplicated, THEN the inventory checker SHALL reject the export.
IF a security-critical mutant survives, THEN the acceptance validator SHALL block the package pending a supported disposition.

phase.steps: Extend or version the existing exporter/checker without weakening old complete-inventory mode. Freeze a producer schema and expected scenario inventory before exporting. Capture actual original requests, complete raw Core results, ordered effects, context, signed policies, evidence, parent/nonce revisions and observed outcomes from executed traces. For each agreement call, independently execute frozen Python and compare every required field. Check cancellation identity and authority history separately: Python Core does not prove signature/nonce correctness. Require every profile/case and detect duplicate, missing, foreign-source, malformed, substituted and concealed rejected records. No --allow-subset acceptance. Preserve independent checker ownership when available and disclose existing shared model/checker authorship. Retain baseline/mutant/report triples for program, projection, payment order, deposit effects, absent-versus-zero choice, rollback time, plan, proof/context, nonce/parent, cancellation and inventory mutations.
phase.acceptance: Full mandatory integrated inventory agrees with the independent checks; every security-critical mutant is rejected or explicitly blocks acceptance. A precomputed expected-result fixture is not an executed export.

phase.title: Obtain honest bounded model-checking evidence

ears_requirements.requirement: WHEN a model is factored, the workstream SHALL preserve the original semantics and compare the complete existing corpus.
WHEN model checking starts, its manifest SHALL declare domains, depth, properties, fairness, tool versions, and resource limits.
WHEN a bounded verification claim is submitted, the validator SHALL require a terminal checker result for each claimed property.
IF checking terminates before state exploration, THEN the workstream SHALL report incomplete verification without claiming an architecture counterexample.
IF factoring removes a mandatory case or property, THEN the reviewer SHALL reject the factoring proposal.

phase.steps: Inspect existing offline manifests before another attempt. The previous flattened input is about93MB and exploded during inlining. Propose and review semantics-preserving factoring of repeated computation/history; retain original source and compare factored/original behavior over the complete corpus. Do not remove invariants, adverse interleavings or mandatory cases merely to obtain a green result. State finite domains, transition depth, terminal/deadlock treatment, fairness assumptions, property list, tool versions and resource limits before each experiment. Reuse the offline route, with compound .qnt.json input where required; do not start a wildcard listener. First verify a small semantically meaningful slice, then the required complete bounded workloads. Keep terminal stdout/stderr, source/tool hashes, elapsed time and the actual checker result. A bounded result is not a universal proof. An OOM, timeout or unsupported translation is an unresolved obligation, not success, a counterexample or grounds for rejecting A. After a failed run, require a concrete changed hypothesis before another expensive run.
phase.acceptance: Required bounded properties have actual terminal verification evidence. If genuinely externally blocked, record the exact gap and complete other authorized work; do not mark A fully complete.

candidate_a_completion_prompt.work_loop: Execute A0 through A7 in dependency order. A2 and A3 may have separate owners after A1; do not edit shared modules concurrently. Factoring research may run alongside lifecycle implementation, but final checks must bind final sources. For each meaningful unit: freeze acceptance and expected observations; retain a compiling behavioral RED with exact source/import bytes; implement minimally; typecheck, test, run positive witnesses and safety predicates; obtain scoped review; fix demonstrated findings; archive once; commit; update durable state; move to the next unfinished deliverable. Parser/type errors are not behavioral RED, and missing original bytes cannot be reconstructed as historical evidence. Keep progress reports focused on delivered behavior and open acceptance gaps. Never describe tool activity alone as completion. Resume the same expensive process after a yielded call; do not create an external background loop unless a supported continuation mechanism actually exists and its status is verified. Exhaust safe in-scope alternatives before an external-blocker handoff. Respect the host's goal/blocker policy and do not invent another authority contract.
candidate_a_completion_prompt.final_response_contract: Report a checklist for A0–A7 with exact source/evidence commits and separately identify implementation, runtime tests, independent correspondence, bounded verification, Council and integration status. List remaining defects and assumptions. If only local technical work is complete, say that rather than “Candidate A fully complete.” Do not imply sampling proves invariants, a symbolic signature is cryptographic verification, or Candidate A selects the architecture. Name the next B–D/S02 work without silently starting unrelated work in this focused handoff session.
